biography.plain_text: John B. Thomson was an American industrialist who became the owner and chairman of Thomson Industries, the precision-motion business founded by his father. An engineering graduate of the New York Institute of Technology, he contributed patents to its products and oversaw acquisitions before selling the company to Danaher in 2002.

long_biography.plain_text:
American industrialist John B. Thomson was also a competitive sailor who preferred racing with amateur crews, often drawn from lifelong friends. He steered his own boats and helped younger sailors develop through a programme that produced Olympians, professional sailors and America's Cup crew members. His racing extended from local dinghy courses to offshore events across several continents.

He founded the Manhasset Bay Fall Series to encourage big-boat racing on western Long Island Sound during its windy autumn season. The regatta's overall trophy honoured his father. He served as commodore of the Storm Trysail Club and was active in the International 50-Foot and Farr 40 class associations.
